key_insight: Microalgae can act as a sustainable sacrificial scavenger that markedly boosts photocatalytic CO2 conversion to CO and CH4 when paired with a polymorphic high-entropy oxide catalyst.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a scalable materials-and-process strategy for greener solar fuel production by coupling engineered HEO photocatalysts with carbon-negative biological CO2 capture.
method: Designed an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs and Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 chemisorption and Bi to promote polarization and charge separation.
Compared photocatalytic CO2 reduction under three conditions: HEO alone, with microplastics, and with microalgae as sacrificial agents.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increased CO and CH4 production by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on maintaining microalgae viability and stable catalyst performance under real reaction conditions, which may be challenging at scale.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
